channel.title: Engineering Digest
channel.description: Daily digest of engineering blog posts from top tech companies

item.title: How Agent Anomaly Detection scores on benchmarks we didn't write
item.description: Agent Anomaly Detection (AAD) provides asynchronous, low-latency monitoring for AI agents by analyzing OpenTelemetry traces and logs to flag goal hijacks and tool misuse Tested across five public security benchmarks, AAD successfully caught 87% of harmful instructions carried out by agents without adding runtime latency Developers can integrate AAD alongside semantic governance and strict tool limits as part of a defense-in-depth strategy to secure agentic applications.

item.title: Catch Go bugs that fuzzing misses with Gemini and a constraint solver
item.description: How pairing Go's surviving compiler bounds-check traps with Gemini 4 Argon and the Z3 constraint solver catches latent out-of-bounds panics in Go code and uncovers a slice-capacity blind spot in go test -fuzz.

item.title: Introducing Spend Management: Spending limits and alerts for Cloudflare
item.description: Spend Management adds opt-in spending caps for Cloudflare Workers and Durable Objects, and more products soon Here is how we built the metering pipeline that turns usage into runtime decisions.

item.title: GitHub availability report: October 2026
item.description: In October, we experienced eight incidents that resulted in degraded performance across GitHub services The post GitHub availability report: October 2026 appeared first on The GitHub Blog.

item.title: Build once, run on any agent: A practical guide to agent skills
item.description: Agent skills capture repeatable engineering work in files teams can review and reuse, while tools, project context, and permissions remain specific to the host that runs them The post Build once, run on any agent: A practical guide to agent skills appeared first on The GitHub Blog.
